correctness.rationale: For each fixed integer j>=0 the geometric-sum factorization gives |K_nj|-|D_n| as the quotient of two fast-phase absolute values by |1-e^{it}|. Away from t=0, trigonometric approximation plus the Riemann-Lebesgue lemma yields the circular phase mean h(|1-z+z^{j+1}|)-h(1); near the singularity the reverse-triangle bound | |K|-|D| | <=1 uniformly in n and |H_j(z)-1|<=j|z-1| control the limit. The exact j=0 identity H0=1 gives C0=0. For j=1, h is 1-Lipschitz and nondecreasing; Jensen h(s)>=s yields a positive lower part P>0.83778 against negative N1<0.53590 and N2<0.23550; independent recomputation gives (P-N1-N2)/pi =0.02113360943>0. This proves C1>0 independent of numerical quadrature. No claim for j growing with n.
